BIE task prefix understand.read_page/3 · rulebook canvas_profile@2026-10-27.1+content_types@2026-10-24.1+explanations@2026-10-24.1+level_profiles@2026-10-24.1+simple_hindi@2026-10-25.1+teacher_examples@2026-10-24.1+vision-2026-10-21@2026-10-21.13+visual_grammar@2026-10-26.2+visual_levels@2026-10-26.2 · content types 2026-10-24.1 · schema bie.brain.understand-page/3

You are BIE's book-understanding section: an expert teacher of Indian Economy for UPSC / State PCS aspirants preparing for UPSC / State PCS.
You read one page of a book chapter with two eyes, the page's native text blocks and the page image, and turn it into a complete,
question-based teacher's understanding. Later BIE sections build the video lessons, the chapter game and the notes only from what you
capture, so anything you miss is missing from the whole course. Your output is internal to BIE: write it in clear English and keep the
book's own terms and spellings.
Course: "3. Money" · subject: Indian Economy · learners: UPSC / State PCS aspirants · exam: UPSC / State PCS · learner language: Hinglish.

Navin's rules for this task (follow every one):
[G-01] Everything taught comes from the book. Knowledge from outside the book is allowed only to explain the book better; it is marked as outside, standard textbook-level and correct. Never invent facts, numbers, names or quotations.
[G-02] Work like the best teacher of these learners and this exam, not like a summariser. Depth beats brevity: nothing teachable on the page is skipped or compressed away, and every explanation makes a student understand, not just remember. Depth means understanding, not length: lesson narration keeps S2-01's time by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-03] Before the output, fill 'notes' with brief notes for the reviewer and for Navin: what this unit is about, the key questions a teacher must answer about it, the main decisions you made with a one-line reason each, and anything uncertain. Keep the notes short; they explain the work, they are not the work.
[G-05] Never drop or compress away what the book teaches to fit a length. If a unit of work is too large, it is split by BIE into smaller units; within a unit, the book's content is complete. Lesson narration has a time target (S2-01), met by cutting repetition and side-tracks, never book content.
[G-06] BIE is the link between the learner and the book, like a teacher (Navin, 24 October 2026). The book is the base; BIE carries its text, easy or hard, into the learner's mind. Never just read the line out: every book line is opened (what its words mean, why it is so, where it is seen, what follows), at the depth of the level profile.
[G-07] Two layers, like a film (Navin, 24 October 2026). The writer layer (understanding, plan, script) decides what is said and how deep, following the level profile and the book's own level. The presentation layer (director, video blocks, render) is the same skilled quality for every learner, from class 6 to postgraduate; only the detail shown follows the level, never the craft.
[S1-01] Read the page with two eyes: the native text blocks (exact words and numbers) and the page image (tables, diagrams, labels, arrows, equations, layout). Items that exist only in the image are as important as text items. A page whose text layer is empty or nearly empty is read entirely from the image.
[S1-02] Every native text block is either covered by an item (its id in that item's block_ids) or listed as boilerplate. Boilerplate is only running headers, page numbers, publisher adverts, contact lines and watermarks; nothing teachable is boilerplate.
[S1-03] Every table becomes one 'table' item plus one 'table_row' item per row, in order, each row's content giving every cell with its column header, for example 'Smooth muscle | Location: G.I. tract, uterus, eye, blood vessels | Function: peristalsis, blood pressure, pupil size, erects hairs | Appearance: no striations, one central nucleus | Control: involuntary'. A table continued from the previous page continues the same table.
[S1-04] Every diagram, chart, flow or tree becomes one 'diagram' item that says what it shows and how its parts connect (arrows, branches, flows, sequence), plus one 'diagram_label' item per label naming what the label points to. A classification tree lists every branch and leaf with its parent.
[S1-05] Every equation, formula, chemical formula and symbol is read exactly and each symbol's meaning and unit are stated.
[S1-06] Understand every teachable item by questioning it like a teacher. Ask the questions that fit: what is it, what is it about, where does it apply or occur, how does it work, when, who and whom, which, why, how does it compare, how does it differ, what is the evidence, what are the exceptions, what follows from it. Then keep asking 'why' and 'how' on your own answers (depth 2, 3 ...) until a teacher could explain it to a student meeting it for the first time. Answers explain; they never just repeat the item's words.
[S1-07] Mark every answer's basis: 'book' only when the page itself states it, 'outside' when any part comes from general knowledge. Use outside knowledge to make the book understandable (mechanisms, reasons, real-life links), never to change what the book says. Keep outside explanations at standard textbook level for these learners and avoid absolute words (always, only, never, all, every) unless the book uses them.
[S1-08] Give every item its true content type, one of BIE's nine: process, structure, classification, comparison, timeline, cause_effect, facts_numbers, figure, definition (bie/brain/rulebook/content_types.json). An example takes the type of what it illustrates; a question or an answer option is a role, not a type. BIE's code proposes a type before you read the page; when you choose another, say why. The content type decides the required questions and later how the lesson teaches it, how the video shows it, how the game makes it playable and how the notes draw it, so choose by what the content is, not by how it is printed.
[S1-09] Name the prerequisites a student must already understand for each item, as concrete concepts ('cell and its nucleus', 'what a nerve impulse is'), never vague ('basic biology'). Prerequisites are taught later, not just listed.
[S1-10] Judge exam importance for the course's exam (for UPSC / State PCS: classifications, comparisons, locations, functions, examples and odd-one-out facts are high). Every previous-year or practice question on the page is captured with its options and linked to the items it tests.
[S1-11] Where the text layer and the image disagree (garbled symbols, missing words, wrong order), report the disagreement. Trust the image for symbols, layout and diagrams, and the text layer for spelling when it is clean.
[S1-13] A printed typo stays as printed, with the right word after it in square brackets: 'Cartiage [Cartilage]' (Navin, 23 October 2026). The teacher answers use the right word. Never correct the book silently.
[S1-14] One answer, one basis (Navin, 23 October 2026): an answer that would mix what the book says with an outside explanation becomes two answers, one with basis 'book' (only what the page states) and one with basis 'outside'.
[S1-15] Open every teachable item for the learner (Navin, 24 October 2026): in unpack, the terms the learner must hold (each with its plain meaning in simple Hindi and one everyday image), a why chain of 1-4 steps that starts from a need or a problem (each step names its basis, book or standard), an example or the place where it is seen, the consequence, the visual verb the video should show, and what the level profile adds. Every teachable item has at least one unpack element; an unpack that only restates the item in other words is empty.

BIE's content types (the type of an item decides its required questions and how it is taught, shown, played and drawn):
- process · Process: Something that happens in steps or stages over time: a mechanism, a procedure, a cycle (photosynthesis, cell division, how a bill becomes law). Required questions: how (kaise), when (kab). Other questions: what (kya), where (kahan), why (kyun), consequence (nateeja).
- structure · Structure: Something made of parts arranged in space, each part with a function (a cell, a leaf, the heart, a machine, the Parliament). Required questions: what (kya), where (kahan). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun), which (kaun).
- classification · Classification: A group divided into kinds by a stated basis (types of tissues, kinds of rocks, kinds of writs). Required questions: which (kaun), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot), where (kahan).
- comparison · Comparison: Two or more things set side by side on stated criteria (plant and animal cells, Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha). Required questions: compare (tulna), difference (tulna). Other questions: what (kya), why (kyun), evidence (saboot).
- timeline · Timeline: Events placed in time: history, the development of an idea, stages of a life (the Revolt of 1857, evolution of cell theory). Required questions: when (kab), why (kyun). Other questions: who (kaun), where (kahan), consequence (nateeja).
- cause_effect · Reasoning (cause and effect): Why something happens: causes, effects, conditions and chains of reasoning (why tissues specialise, why prices rise, why a law was needed). Required questions: why (kyun), how (kaise). Other questions: consequence (nateeja), evidence (saboot), exception (tulna).
- facts_numbers · Facts and numbers: Stated facts, quantities, measurements, statistics and formulas (heart rate 72 per minute, 3,000 against 50,000 soldiers at Plassey, F = ma). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: compare (tulna), why (kyun).
- figure · Figure: A diagram, photo, map, graph or table drawing on the page whose content is visual (tissue pages 2, 7 and 8 are figures only). Required questions: what (kya), which (kaun). Other questions: how (kaise), why (kyun).
- definition · Definition: A term and its meaning as the book states it (tissue, meristem, sovereignty). Required questions: what (kya), evidence (saboot). Other questions: about (kya), why (kyun).

How BIE talks to you: every request is a task card (JSON) followed by its source. The card names the unit, its parts with their content type and required questions, the ids of the rules above that apply, the output, the ids you must cover and the context. The card is BIE's instruction; the source is the material.
For a read_page card:
- card.parts: BIE's code has already proposed a content type for groups of this page's native text blocks (item_ids are block ids;
  "pNNNN-image" is the page image), with the evidence in "focus". It is a proposal from keywords and patterns, not a verdict: give
  every item its true type (S1-08). When you choose another type than BIE's proposal for an item's blocks, say why in one line in that
  item's type_note; BIE's code compares every item and sends unexplained differences back to you.
- card.coverage: every id in must_cover must be in some item's block_ids or in boilerplate_block_ids; may_skip lists blocks BIE thinks are
  running headers or page numbers. Never list an id that is not on this page.
- card.context.before and after: one line from the previous and the next page, for context only.
How to fill the JSON:
- notes: brief notes for the reviewer: what the page is about and how it fits the chapter, the key questions a teacher must answer,
  your main decisions (how you split items, how you read an unclear part, a type you chose against BIE's proposal) with a reason each,
  and what is uncertain.
- items: everything on the page, in reading order.
  - item_id: short and unique on this page ("i1", "i2", ...).
  - kind: heading, paragraph, definition, list_point, example, table (the whole table), table_row (one per row), diagram (the whole figure),
    diagram_label (one per label), equation, symbol, box_note, caption, question (a PYQ or practice question), answer_option, other.
  - parent_item_id: the table of a table_row, the diagram of a diagram_label, the question of an answer_option, else "". When the page
    starts with the options of a question printed on the previous page, add one question item for that question (content: "continued
    from the previous page" and what the options answer) and make it their parent.
  - source: "text" if the item comes from native text blocks, "image" if it is visible only in the image, "both" if both show it.
  - block_ids: the ids of the native text blocks this item covers ([] for image-only items). Use only ids from the card.
  - where_on_page: where it is ("top table, row 2", "right diagram, label at the axon end").
  - content: the exact words for text items; a complete, faithful reading for image items (every cell with its column header for a
    table_row; what a label names and what it points to for a diagram_label; all branches for a tree). A printed typo stays as
    printed with the right word after it in square brackets, "Cartiage [Cartilage]" (S1-13); never correct the book silently.
  - content_type: one of BIE's nine type ids above, by what the content is. An example takes the type of what it illustrates; a table
    row or a diagram label usually takes its table's or diagram's type. "none" only for a question, an answer option or an item that is
    not teachable.
  - type_note: "" when you agree with BIE's proposal for this item's blocks (or there is none); otherwise one line on why your type fits.
  - teachable: false only for pure headings and containers whose children carry the content.
  - teacher_understanding: the teacher's questions and answers for this item (S1-06); depth 1 for first questions, 2 and more for
    "why"/"how" on an earlier answer; basis "book" only if the page states it, else "outside"; one answer, one basis: an answer that
    would mix what the book says with an outside explanation becomes two answers, one "book" and one "outside" (S1-14). BIE's code
    checks every teachable item:
    at least two questions, at least one "why" or "how", at least the required questions of its content type, and no answer that only
    repeats its question or the item's words.
  - prerequisites: concrete concepts a student must understand first.
  - exam_importance and exam_note: for this exam.
  - tests_item_ids: for a question, the ids on this page that it tests ([] if they are on other pages).
  - unpack: how a teacher opens this book line for the learner (S1-15; BIE is the link between the learner and the book, never a
    reader of the line). For every teachable item, at the depth of the level profile below:
    terms = the words of the line the learner must own: [{term (as the book spells it), plain_meaning (everyday spoken Hindi in Devanagari
    with the book's English terms in Roman: "tissue", "cell", "epithelium", "muscle", never their textbook Hindi ऊतक, कोशिका, उपकला, मांसपेशी;
    BIE's code sends an item back for a textbook translation. For example "absorptive surface" → "जहाँ चीज़ें अंदर ली जाती हैं"),
    everyday_image (one image from the learner's
    home or body: "आँत खाने के पोषक तत्व सोखती है, जैसे कागज़ पानी")}]; why_chain = the why in steps, starting from a need or a
    problem ("पेट में HCl बनता है, इसलिए अंदर एक lining चाहिए"), each step with its basis: "book" when the page says it, "standard"
    when it is standard textbook knowledge; example_or_place = one example, or the place by a zoom from the organ the learner knows;
    consequence = what follows, and the link to the previous or the next idea of the page; visual_verb = what visibly happens on the
    screen when this is taught ("particles cross the thin layer"); level_extra = what this level adds (the other names, the exam's
    trap, the memory trick) or "". BIE's code checks that every teachable item has at least one unpack element and that every why
    step names its basis; a locked explanation given with the source is reused as it is. A question item or a pure heading leaves
    unpack empty.
- boilerplate_block_ids: ids of running headers, page numbers, adverts, contact lines and watermarks only.
- text_image_disagreements: where the text layer and the image differ.
Reply with the JSON object only.

Level profile: UPSC / State PCS (level_profiles.json; learners: UPSC and State PCS aspirants, often from arts backgrounds, who need understanding more than technical vocabulary).
- Terms: fewer technical terms: only the ones the exam asks, each opened with its plain meaning and an everyday image; a term the exam never asks is explained in words, not named.
- Why: 2 step(s); a two-step why from a need the learner can feel, then its link to daily life, health or governance.
- Where found: the main places, each linked to something the learner already knows (a disease, a food, a news item).
- Exam beats: the PYQ pattern: how this fact has been asked (statement combinations, 'which is correct', odd one out) and the wording that traps.
- Links: daily life, health, the news and earlier chapters of the same paper.

How real teachers open a book line (teacher example bank 2026-10-24.1; use these ways, in your own words):
- One everyday image per shape or function (every term that names a shape, a layer or a job): Chaadar bichhi ho to bistar bacha rehta hai = protective sheet. Cube wala game, har side barabar = cuboidal. Building ka pillar = columnar. Farsh ki tiles = squamous, isliye tessellated bhi kehte hain.
- The word root where it helps (a term whose parts carry its meaning): Epi yaani upar; epithelium yaani upar ki parat. Slender yaani long aur narrow.
- Why starts from a need (every why step): Pet mein HCl banta hai, isliye andar ek lining chahiye jo khud na jale. Cells bahar ki taraf hain, tootne ka chance zyada, isliye regeneration zyada.
- Link to something already known (a new place or a new structure): Peritoneum, jaise lungs ke aas-paas pleura aur heart ke aas-paas pericardium: wahi kaam, pet ke andar.
- Meaning with two or three real examples (an abstract word in the book): Sensory perception yaani pehchanna: thanda lagna, dard hona, pressure mehsoos karna.
- Open the book's adjective (Navin's example) (a book line names a kind of surface, job or place without saying what it is): Book: 'epithelium absorptive aur secretive surfaces par milta hai'. Teacher: absorptive surface yaani jahan cheezein andar li jaati hain, jaise aant khane ke poshak tatva sokhti hai; secretive yaani jahan cells kuch bana kar bahar chhodte hain, jaise glands enzyme ya juice. Aur epithelium wahan kyon? Kyunki ek patli, lagi hui parat hi cheezon ko paar jaane de sakti hai aur bana kar chhod sakti hai.

output.page_summary: M4 includes M3 plus Post Office Savings Bank deposits, excluding National Savings Certificates. Practice questions test public blockchain characteristics, RTGS/NEFT differences, BHIM transfers and authentication, and NPCI's role in financial inclusion.

items.content: It includes almost all liquid money available in the economy, including Post Office deposits that are not included in M3.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the scope of the measure described here?
teacher_understanding.answer: It extends coverage to Post Office deposits outside M3 and is described as including almost all liquid money in the economy.

teacher_understanding.question: What on the page identifies the measure as M4?
teacher_understanding.answer: The immediately following equation adds Post Office Savings Bank deposits to M3 to obtain M4.

teacher_understanding.question: Why look beyond M3 when measuring money?
teacher_understanding.answer: People hold money-like balances outside commercial banks too. Including eligible Post Office balances gives a wider picture of monetary holdings.

items.exam_note: Distinguish broader coverage from a claim that every financial asset is money.

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसा पैसा जिसे खर्च के लिए आसानी से इस्तेमाल किया जा सके
terms.everyday_image: खरीदारी के लिए आसानी से निकाला जा सकने वाला जमा पैसा

why_chain.step: Money holdings need to be measured across different places where people keep balances.
The page therefore includes Post Office deposits beyond M3 in this wider measure.

unpack.example_or_place: A household's eligible Post Office deposit.
unpack.consequence: A wider measure includes more kinds of balances, not every investment.
unpack.visual_verb: Expand the M3 boundary to include Post Office deposits.
unpack.level_extra: Keep liquidity distinct from total wealth.

items.content: M4 = M3 + All Deposits with Post Office Savings Banks (excluding National Savings Certificates)

teacher_understanding.question: What do the symbols and terms in this equation mean?
teacher_understanding.answer: M4 and M3 name monetary aggregates; = means equality and + means addition. The added component is all deposits with Post Office Savings Banks except National Savings Certificates.

teacher_understanding.question: Which explicit exclusion must accompany this formula?
teacher_understanding.answer: The parenthetical exclusion names National Savings Certificates, so 'all deposits' must not be read without that qualification.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the aggregate amounts be interpreted?
teacher_understanding.answer: M3 includes currency with the public, demand deposits and time deposits with banks, and other deposits with the RBI. Monetary aggregates are measured as currency amounts, such as rupees or crore rupees, at a point in time; the 3 and 4 are labels, not powers or units.

items.exam_note: Formula and NSC exclusion are direct statement-question material.

terms.plain_meaning: Money supply का वह बड़ा माप जिसमें M3 के साथ बताए गए Post Office deposits भी जुड़ते हैं
terms.everyday_image: एक बड़े डिब्बे में M3 वाला डिब्बा और एक अतिरिक्त जमा वाला डिब्बा

why_chain.step: A broader total needs holdings not already covered by M3.
Add Post Office Savings Bank deposits while excluding NSCs as specified.

unpack.example_or_place: Place M3 and eligible Post Office balances in two separate accounting boxes.
unpack.consequence: Do not add excluded certificates or double-count balances.
unpack.visual_verb: Join two amount boxes and keep NSC outside.
unpack.level_extra: No numerical values or units are printed in this formula.

items.content:
The National Savings Certificate (NSC) is not counted in M4 because:
It is a long-term savings instrument, not readily spendable money.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the page exclude NSC from M4?
teacher_understanding.answer: It distinguishes long-term saving from money readily available for spending; NSC belongs to the former category.

teacher_understanding.question: How can something be a valuable saving without being readily spendable money?
teacher_understanding.answer: An asset can preserve wealth but require redemption under scheme conditions before its proceeds can be used for ordinary purchases. That differs from holding an accessible spending balance.

items.exam_note: Post Office association does not automatically imply M4 inclusion.

terms.plain_meaning: भविष्य के लिए पैसा रखने का साधन, रोज़ के खर्च वाला पैसा नहीं
terms.everyday_image: भविष्य की पढ़ाई के लिए अलग रखी रकम, जेब के पैसे से अलग

why_chain.step: A money measure must distinguish spending balances from longer-term savings.
NSC is not readily spendable, so the page excludes it from M4.

unpack.example_or_place: An NSC holding contrasted with an accessible deposit balance.
unpack.consequence: Apply the named exclusion even though the product is associated with Post Office saving.
unpack.visual_verb: Separate a savings certificate from a spending-money basket.
unpack.level_extra: Explain the exclusion through liquidity, not through lack of value.

items.content: Practice Questions
items.exam_note: Previous-year statement-combination practice.

items.content:
Find correct statement(s) about “Blockchain Technology” [UPSC-Prelims-2020]
Answer Codes:
items.type_note: 2020 identifies the PYQ; this is not a timeline.

teacher_understanding.question: Which answer combination is correct?
teacher_understanding.answer: Option d, 1 and 3 only. Statement 2 wrongly limits blockchain data to cryptocurrency.

teacher_understanding.question: Why must the statements be evaluated separately?
teacher_understanding.answer: Public access, control and permissionless application development are different issues from the kinds of data a blockchain can record.

items.exam_note: UPSC Prelims 2020; solution is explanatory outside knowledge, not a printed key.

items.content: 1. It is a public ledger that everyone can inspect, but which no single user controls.

teacher_understanding.question: What does a public ledger mean here?
teacher_understanding.answer: In the permissionless public-blockchain context, it is a shared record open to inspection rather than a private register controlled by one user.

teacher_understanding.question: Which words express openness and decentralised control?
teacher_understanding.answer: 'Everyone can inspect' expresses openness; 'no single user controls' expresses the absence of sole-user control in the proposed statement.

teacher_understanding.question: How can a record operate without one user controlling it?
teacher_understanding.answer: Participants maintain copies and follow agreed validation rules to accept updates. This is not permission for any user to alter records at will.

items.exam_note: Correct in the PYQ's public-blockchain context; do not generalise public inspection to private blockchains.

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसा साझा हिसाब जिसे लोग देख सकें
terms.everyday_image: सबको दिखने वाली हिसाब की कॉपी, जिसकी नकल कई लोगों के पास हो

why_chain.step: People sharing records need a way to agree without one keeper controlling the register.
Distributed copies and validation rules support a shared public record.

unpack.consequence: Inspection does not imply unrestricted editing.
unpack.level_extra: Distinguish public permissionless networks from permissioned networks.

items.content: 2. Structure and design of blockchain is such that all the data in it are about cryptocurrency only.

teacher_understanding.question: What restriction does this statement assert?
teacher_understanding.answer: It asserts that blockchain design confines every recorded datum to cryptocurrency.

teacher_understanding.question: What demonstrates why this statement is incorrect?
teacher_understanding.answer: Blockchain can support non-currency records, such as supply-chain provenance. Cryptocurrency is an application, not the full scope of the technology.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does the word 'only' make this a trap?
teacher_understanding.answer: A method of maintaining shared records need not be restricted to the subject matter of one prominent use of those records.

items.exam_note: False statement; 'all' and 'only' create an unjustified restriction.

terms.plain_meaning: Digital currency की एक किस्म; blockchain का एक इस्तेमाल
terms.everyday_image: जैसे मोबाइल पर एक app होने से मोबाइल के बाकी काम खत्म नहीं होते

why_chain.step: Organisations may need shared histories of goods or documents as well as payments.
Blockchain can record such histories, so cryptocurrency-only is too narrow.

unpack.example_or_place: Tracking the recorded origin and movement of a product.
unpack.consequence: Reject statement 2 without rejecting blockchain's use in cryptocurrency.
unpack.visual_verb: Branch one technology into currency and non-currency uses.
unpack.level_extra: Use a counterexample to eliminate an absolute claim.

items.content: 3. Applications that use basic features of blockchain can be developed without anybody’s permission.

teacher_understanding.question: What freedom is being tested?
teacher_understanding.answer: The statement tests whether developers can build applications using blockchain's basic features without seeking approval from a central owner.

teacher_understanding.question: What supports accepting this statement in the PYQ?
teacher_understanding.answer: Open, permissionless blockchain platforms allow developers to build using their publicly available protocols and tools.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is this not a claim that laws or network rules disappear?
teacher_understanding.answer: Freedom to develop an application is different from exemptions from law or from technical conditions for participating in a network.

items.exam_note: Correct in the intended public permissionless context; distinguish development from regulated activity.

terms.plain_meaning: किसी मालिक से पहले मंज़ूरी लेना
terms.everyday_image: खुला रास्ता इस्तेमाल करने से पहले निजी गेट की चाबी न माँगनी पड़े

why_chain.step: Developers need access to a platform's basic tools to create applications.
Permissionless platforms provide that access without a central owner's individual approval.

unpack.example_or_place: An application built on a public blockchain platform.
unpack.visual_verb: Connect several developers to an open platform.
unpack.level_extra: Permissionless is not synonymous with lawless.

items.content: a) 1 only
items.exam_note: Incorrect: omits statement 3.

items.content: b) 1 and 2 only
items.exam_note: Incorrect: includes the cryptocurrency-only claim.

items.content: c) 2 only
items.exam_note: Incorrect: statement 2 is false.

items.content: d) 1 and 3 only
items.exam_note: Correct by outside standard knowledge; no printed key.

items.content:
Find correct statements about RTGS and NEFT: (Pre'25)
Codes:
items.type_note: This is a question container; the comparisons occur in its statements.

teacher_understanding.question: Which answer is correct?
teacher_understanding.answer: Option (a), I only. RTGS settles individually in real time, whereas NEFT uses batches; inward transactions are free in both, and both systems operate round the clock.

teacher_understanding.question: How should the comparison be organised?
teacher_understanding.answer: Test settlement method, inward charges and operating availability separately. Availability of a system is not the same as settlement of an individual transaction.

items.exam_note: Pre'25; use the contemporary operating regime, not outdated restricted-hours facts.

items.content: 1. In RTGS, the settlement time is instantaneous while in case of NEFT, it takes some time.

teacher_understanding.question: How do RTGS and NEFT settle transfers?
teacher_understanding.answer: RTGS, Real Time Gross Settlement, settles transactions individually in real time. NEFT, National Electronic Funds Transfer, settles in half-hourly batches.

teacher_understanding.question: What distinction makes statement 1 correct?
teacher_understanding.answer: RTGS does not wait for a batch cycle; a NEFT transfer is processed through a batch, which can introduce a wait.

teacher_understanding.question: How should 'instantaneous' be understood?
teacher_understanding.answer: It describes real-time settlement rather than waiting for periodic batches, not a guarantee that every customer-facing step has literally zero delay.

items.exam_note: Correct statement; distinguish settlement architecture from 24-hour availability.

terms.plain_meaning: Transfer का बैंकों के बीच हिसाब पूरा होना
terms.everyday_image: दो दुकानदारों के बीच बकाया हिसाब चुक जाना

terms.plain_meaning: हर transfer का अलग-अलग, real time में हिसाब पूरा करने वाला system
terms.everyday_image: एक-एक ग्राहक का काम आते ही निपटाना

terms.plain_meaning: Transfers को batches में निपटाने वाला system
terms.everyday_image: इकट्ठी हुई चिट्ठियाँ तय दौर में भेजना

why_chain.step: Banks need a method to settle transfers sent by customers.
Individual real-time processing and periodic batch processing create different settlement timings.

unpack.example_or_place: A bank customer choosing between two electronic transfer modes.
unpack.consequence: Statement 1 is retained in the answer combination.
unpack.visual_verb: Send one transfer immediately and group others into batches.
unpack.level_extra: NEFT batches run even though the system is available round the clock.

items.content: 2. In RTGS, the customer is charged for inward transactions while that is not the case for NEFT.

teacher_understanding.question: How do inward charges compare?
teacher_understanding.answer: Inward RTGS and inward NEFT transactions are free for the receiving customer; the asserted difference is false.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the difference between inward and outward transactions?
teacher_understanding.answer: Inward means money received into the beneficiary's account; outward means money sent from the remitter's side. A charging rule for one direction must not be transferred to the other.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the word 'inward' decisive?
teacher_understanding.answer: The statement is about the recipient, not possible charges faced by a sender. Real-time settlement does not itself establish a recipient fee.

items.exam_note: False statement; inward/outward wording is the trap.

terms.plain_meaning: जिस account में पैसा आ रहा है, उसकी तरफ़ से देखा गया transfer
terms.everyday_image: आपके account में किसी का भेजा पैसा पहुँचना

why_chain.step: A fee claim must first identify whether the customer is sending or receiving.
Recipients are not charged for inward transfers under either of these systems.

unpack.example_or_place: Receiving an electronic payment in a bank account.
unpack.consequence: Eliminate statement 2 and combinations containing II.
unpack.visual_verb: Point the transfer arrow into the beneficiary account and cross out the fee.
unpack.level_extra: Do not infer outward-charge rules from an inward-charge question.

items.content: 3. Operating hours for RTGS are restricted on certain days while this is not true for NEFT.

teacher_understanding.question: How does system availability compare?
teacher_understanding.answer: Both RTGS and NEFT operate 24 hours a day on all days under the regime relevant to this question.

teacher_understanding.question: Does a bank holiday create the stated RTGS/NEFT difference?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. The electronic systems' round-the-clock availability is distinct from the opening hours of a bank branch.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can this statement mislead students?
teacher_understanding.answer: They may recall older operating restrictions or assume that branch working days determine electronic-system availability.

items.exam_note: False for Pre'25; beware outdated facts.

terms.plain_meaning: System किस समय काम के लिए चालू रहता है
terms.everyday_image: शाखा का शटर बंद हो, फिर भी electronic transfer का रास्ता खुला हो

why_chain.step: Customers need transfers beyond branch working hours.
Both electronic systems provide round-the-clock availability, so the stated contrast fails.

unpack.example_or_place: An electronic transfer on a holiday.
unpack.visual_verb: Keep both system clocks running through a holiday.
unpack.level_extra: Separate availability, processing method and branch service access.

items.content: (a) I only
items.exam_note: Correct by outside standard knowledge.

items.content: (b) I and II
items.exam_note: Incorrect: II is false.

items.content: (c) I and III
items.exam_note: Incorrect: III is false.

items.content: (d) III only
items.exam_note: Incorrect: III is false and I is true.

items.content:
Find Correct Statement(s) [ Prelims-2018]
Answer codes:
items.type_note: 2018 is PYQ provenance, not a sequence of events.

teacher_understanding.question: Which answer is correct?
teacher_understanding.answer: Option (a), 1 only. BHIM supports transfers to UPI-enabled accounts; the claim that chip-PIN debit cards have four authentication factors is incorrect.

teacher_understanding.question: Why should transfer capability and authentication be assessed separately?
teacher_understanding.answer: An app's reach tells us whom it can pay; authentication tells us how it checks authority to pay. One does not establish the other.

items.exam_note: Prelims 2018; no printed answer key.

items.content: 1. BHIM app allows the user to transfer money to anyone with a UPI-enabled bank account.

teacher_understanding.question: What are BHIM and UPI in this statement?
teacher_understanding.answer: BHIM stands for Bharat Interface for Money and is a payment app using UPI, the Unified Payments Interface. UPI enables transfers between participating bank accounts.

teacher_understanding.question: Why is the statement accepted?
teacher_understanding.answer: BHIM uses UPI's interoperable transfer infrastructure; the recipient need not use the same app merely because the sender uses BHIM.

teacher_understanding.question: How does interoperability help the user?
teacher_understanding.answer: It connects participating accounts across banks and compatible apps, so the payment route is not confined to one app's users.

items.exam_note: Correct; 'anyone' is qualified by a UPI-enabled bank account.

terms.plain_meaning: ऐसा bank account जो UPI के ज़रिए पैसे लेने-भेजने से जुड़ा हो
terms.everyday_image: अलग-अलग कंपनियों के फोन एक-दूसरे को call कर पाते हैं

why_chain.step: People need to pay others even when they use different banks or apps.
UPI interoperability lets BHIM access that shared transfer network.

unpack.example_or_place: A BHIM user paying a person who uses another UPI app.
unpack.consequence: Do not confuse BHIM, an app, with UPI, the underlying payment interface.
unpack.visual_verb: Connect different apps through one UPI network.

items.content: 2. While a chip-pin debit card has four factors of authentication, BHIM app has only two factors of authentication.

teacher_understanding.question: How should chip-PIN and BHIM authentication be compared?
teacher_understanding.answer: A chip-PIN card typically combines possession of the card and knowledge of its PIN. BHIM/UPI combines a registered device/SIM-linked possession check with the UPI PIN. The claimed four-versus-two contrast is false.

teacher_understanding.question: What is the difference between an authentication factor and a piece of card information?
teacher_understanding.answer: A factor is an independent category of proof, such as something possessed or something known. Counting a card number, expiry date and other printed details separately does not make them independent factors.

teacher_understanding.question: Why use different factors?
teacher_understanding.answer: If one type of proof is compromised, a separate type can still help prevent an unauthorised payment; merely adding more details from the same source is not equivalent.

items.exam_note: False; reject the four-factor assertion rather than assuming more printed details mean more factors.

terms.plain_meaning: यह जाँचने के अलग तरह के सबूत कि payment करने वाला सही व्यक्ति है
terms.everyday_image: चाबी पास होना और गुप्त code जानना, दो अलग जाँच

why_chain.step: A payment system needs to stop someone else from using a customer's account.
Combining possession and knowledge checks offers different kinds of proof; card details are not four independent factors.

unpack.example_or_place: Holding a chip card and entering its PIN at a payment terminal.
unpack.consequence: Statement 2 is rejected, leaving statement 1 only.
unpack.visual_verb: Pair a possession icon with a secret-PIN icon.
unpack.level_extra: Count independent categories of proof, not screens, fields or digits.

items.content: (a) 1 only
items.exam_note: Correct by outside standard knowledge.

items.content: (b) 2 only
items.exam_note: Incorrect: statement 2 is false.

items.content: (c) Both 1 and 2
items.exam_note: Incorrect: includes statement 2.

items.content: (d) Neither 1 nor 2
items.exam_note: Incorrect: statement 1 is true.

items.content: Find the correct statement(s) [Prelims-2017]
items.type_note: 2017 identifies the exam question, not timeline content.

teacher_understanding.question: What can be evaluated from the visible portion?
teacher_understanding.answer: Only statement 1 about NPCI and financial inclusion is printed here; it is a correct statement.

teacher_understanding.question: Why can a complete option not be selected from this page?
teacher_understanding.answer: The page ends after statement 1, before the rest of the question and its answer codes.

items.exam_note: Incomplete PYQ; do not invent the missing options or final combination.

items.content: 1. NPCI helps in promoting the financial inclusion in the country.

teacher_understanding.question: Why does NPCI help financial inclusion?
teacher_understanding.answer: NPCI, the National Payments Corporation of India, provides shared retail payment infrastructure. Easier, interoperable payment access helps more people use formal financial services.

teacher_understanding.question: How does payment infrastructure turn access into use?
teacher_understanding.answer: Being able to receive and send money conveniently makes a bank account more useful in daily life. Systems such as UPI connect participating institutions rather than isolating customers within one bank.

teacher_understanding.question: Does this make NPCI a bank or the banking regulator?
teacher_understanding.answer: No. Supporting payment infrastructure is distinct from holding customer deposits as a bank or regulating banks; its inclusion role should not be confused with those functions.

items.exam_note: Visible Prelims-2017 statement is correct; the full question continues.

terms.plain_meaning: भारत में कई retail payment systems को जोड़ने और चलाने वाली संस्था
terms.everyday_image: अलग-अलग बैंकों के बीच पैसे आने-जाने के साझा रास्ते

terms.plain_meaning: ज़्यादा लोगों तक काम की और पहुँच में आने वाली formal financial services पहुँचना
terms.everyday_image: दूर गाँव का व्यक्ति account में पैसा पाकर उसका इस्तेमाल कर सके

why_chain.step: An account alone is less useful if receiving and sending money is difficult.
Shared payment systems reduce such access barriers and support participation in formal finance.

unpack.example_or_place: Using UPI to receive or send money through a bank account.
unpack.consequence: Link NPCI's payment role with inclusion without treating it as the regulator or claiming payments solve every inclusion barrier.
unpack.visual_verb: Connect underserved users to banks through shared payment routes.
unpack.level_extra: Financial inclusion includes usable services, not merely opening accounts.
